final_answer:
Let
\[
Q_s(p)=\bigl(d_s(i,j)^p-d_s(i,\ast)^p-d_s(j,\ast)^p\bigr)_{0\le i,j\le 12}.
\]
Then \(p\)-negative type is equivalent to \(Q_s(p)\le 0\).

At \(s=0,p=1\), the null vector in the zero-sum coordinates is
\[
u=(-2,1,0,0,2,-2,-2,0,2,0,0,1,-2),
\]
corresponding to
\[
(a_0,\ldots,a_{12},a_\ast)=(-2,1,0,0,2,-2,-2,0,2,0,0,1,-2,2).
\]
One checks
\[
Q_0(1)u=0,\qquad u^Tu=26.
\]
On the quotient \(u^\perp\), an exact \(LDL^T\) certificate has diagonal entries
\[
-8,-\frac{55}{2},-\frac{432}{55},-8,-\frac{296}{27},
-\frac{586}{37},-6,-\frac{5531}{879},
-\frac{34280}{5531},-\frac{11222}{4285},
-\frac{14128}{5611},-\frac{2197}{883},
\]
so \(Q_0(1)\) is negative semidefinite with one-dimensional kernel. Also
\[
\frac14\left.\frac{d}{dp}\right|_{p=1}
\sum_{z,w}a_za_wd_0(z,w)^p=\tau>0.
\]
Thus for \(p>1\) close to \(1\), the null direction becomes positive, while \(p<1\) is allowed by the Bernstein-function closure \(x\mapsto x^p\). Hence
\[
\wp(0)=1.
\]

For \(s>0\), writing \(Q_s(1)=Q_0+sA_1+s^2A_2\), standard simple-kernel perturbation gives
\[
\mu_1=\mu_2=0,\qquad \mu_3=-\frac{126}{2197}
\]
for the eigenvalue bifurcating from \(0\). Since
\[
\partial_p\mu(0,1)=\frac{4\tau}{u^Tu}=\frac{2\tau}{13},
\]
we get
\[
\wp(s)=1+\frac{63}{169\tau}s^3+O(s^4),
\]
so
\[
\beta_+=\tau\wp'''(0^+)=\tau\cdot\frac{378}{169\tau}
=\frac{378}{169}.
\]

For \(s<0\), put \(x=-s>0\). The same computation gives
\[
\mu_1=\mu_2=0,\qquad \mu_3=-\frac{99}{4394},
\]
so
\[
\wp(-x)=1+\frac{99}{676\tau}x^3+O(x^4).
\]
Therefore
\[
\wp'''(0^-)=-\frac{297}{338\tau},
\qquad
\beta_-=-\frac{297}{338}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(\wp(0),\beta_-,\beta_+\right)
=\left(1,-\frac{297}{338},\frac{378}{169}\right)}.
\]
